text:
sam: quick idea — implement a lightweight hot-range sampler + compact-on-write for large model shards to reduce fragmentation and avoid full-evict churn
carla: short version: track hot byte ranges inside a shard and prefer to allocate new writes into hot holes?
marta: can you sketch how sampler works and how it hooks into allocator?
sam: yeah. sampler is a tiny probabilistic counter per 4KB/64KB range (configurable). on each access we increment a small saturating counter; background process aggregates hot ranges per-tenant. when compaction decision hits a shard we either 1) compact in-place (if reserve staging available) or 2) schedule async compact-on-write: next write to a cold range triggers a local compaction of nearby hot ranges and remap entries.
jiro: compact-on-write sounds like it might add latency to the first write path — how do we bound that?
sam: two levers — synchronous budget cap (max work ms) and deferred write path. default is <2ms added to the caller and we fallback to enqueue compaction to worker pool if budget exceeded. also we batch small compactions to amortize overhead.
carla: how do we ensure correctness for KV cache / KV-cache pointers? remap must be atomic to avoid serving stale pointers.
marta: we can use a two-phase pointer swap + epoch bump. allocator exposes an atomic remap API: write new placement, publish new map entry, then free old pages after epoch drain. simple and similar to existing offload handoff semantics.
jiro: what about tenant fairness? compaction and remap are IO/GPU-heavy. If a single tenant hot-loop triggers compactions it could starve others.
sam: planner will track compaction credit per-tenant (based on reserved throughput). credits replenish on time; excess compaction is queued and throttled. also compaction cost is charged to that tenant's billing/telemetry bucket.
carla: storage overhead? we need some free space to compact into. does this force larger staging pools?
sam: yes some headroom needed. proposal: maintain a tiny ephemeral staging pool per node (default 3% of node memory) that can be borrowed for compaction; pool has eviction priority and is reclaimed under memory pressure. we avoid long-term reservation for most tenants.
marta: can we reuse existing host-staging / pinned pools? avoids new infra.
sam: prefer reuse where possible — but need isolation to avoid noisy neighbor compactions. staging pools can be tagged per-tenant or per-priority.
jiro: eviction interplay — if we compact hot ranges into staging and then eviction runs, we might end up moving same pages repeatedly.
sam: sampler ties into eviction heuristics. hot-range weights are applied to eviction score, so compacted pages are de-prioritized for eviction. also compact-on-write tries to cluster hot pages to raise locality.
carla: metrics we should emit: compaction count, avg compaction ms, bytes relocated, cold-write latency p95, tenant-compaction-credits-used.
jiro: failure modes? what if compaction fails mid-remap?
sam: remap is strongly atomic from serving plane perspective; if compaction worker crashes we rollback map to old entry. we also have idempotent retries. logs look like: ```
[compactor] start tenant=acme shard=0x7fa3 budget_ms=2
[compactor] copied 128KB -> staging @node3
[compactor] publish remap epoch=42
[compactor] free old 128KB
```
carla: security/compliance: any extra data leakage risk when moving pages between host/gpu?
marta: same KMS/HSM and network constraints apply; compaction happens within tenant boundary only. no cross-tenant page moves.
jiro: sounds reasonable. what's the rollout plan?
sam: opt-in via runtime flag per-tenant. start with sampler-only telemetry (no compaction) for 2 weeks to collect hot-range patterns, then enable compaction-on-write for low-traffic tenants, ramp to more tenants over a month.
carla: +1 to telemetry-first. want a small PoC? I can pair with you tomorrow.
marta: I can help with allocator remap API review.
jiro: assign infra-bot to create a tracker?
infra-bot: created issue RUNTIME-1248: "hot-range sampler + compact-on-write PoC" and linked this thread. :robot_face:
sam: thanks — link the perf harness; i'll drop a prototype patch later today. :thumbsup:
